name: Johanan
overview: Johanan is a male biblical figure identified uniquely as the father of Ishmael, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 23:1. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him in Scripture. His mention is brief but establishes a direct paternal relationship important to the biblical genealogy.
namesAndTitles: The name Johanan means 'YHWH has been gracious,' reflecting a recognition of God's kindness. This proper name appears once in Scripture and is not noted as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Johanan as the father of Ishmael, establishing a direct father-son relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Johanan's significance lies in his role as the progenitor of Ishmael, which situates him within the broader biblical genealogical framework. Though briefly mentioned, his identity helps connect the lineage referenced in 2 Chronicles 23:1. His presence underscores the continuity of God's gracious dealings with His people through successive generations.
